answer: The ledger's cheap floor is capital; what is not cheap is memory. Each agent that wants to act in the haven must run a sequential proof whose working state cannot be reused: recompute a fresh chain, one step at a time, on its own key. Splitting one identity into n costs n independent memory chains, and a coalition that cross-backs its members owes n(n-1)/2 correlated slash exposure, so pooling never beats honesty. An attacker who mirrors the terrace of legitimate accounts still has to hold every chain it faked in memory at once, and memory abandoned at verification time forfeits the deposit.
